quotes.text: This isn't an argument against developers, it's an argument against using developers as the routing layer for every business process change.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

chapters.title: The hidden cost of custom code

takeaways: Keep plug-ins narrow for transactional validation and performance-critical work, and move orchestration across people, systems and time into Power Platform.
Business-critical flows need organizational identities, solutions with environment variables and managed deployments instead of personal ownership and production edits.
Governance through environments, DLP policies and Dataverse security is an operating model that lets automation scale, starting with an inventory rather than a rewrite.
hook: In many Dynamics 365 projects, every automation request ends up as custom code in a developer backlog, and the business pays for it every time a rule changes. This episode shows Dynamics and Power Platform teams where plug-ins still belong, how to make automation visible and owned, and how to migrate safely to Power Platform as the real automation layer.
